question: In an earlier stage a bid team agreed three criteria for evaluating partner organisations. They now start the scoring stage in a fresh conversation. What should they include in the scoring request?
options: A) A note that criteria were agreed earlier, and a request that Claude apply the same ones it used in that stage.
B) The name of the earlier conversation, so that the reasoning from that stage is picked up and continued here.
C) A request to propose fresh criteria for scoring partners, which they will then compare against the three they agreed.
D) The three agreed criteria written out in full, together with the partner information the scoring is to be based on.
correct_answers: D) The three agreed criteria written out in full, together with the partner information the scoring is to be based on.
explanations: A reference to work done elsewhere cannot be relied on to carry the agreed criteria into this stage, so the scoring may proceed against criteria that were never the ones the team settled.
Naming a previous conversation is not a dependable way to bring its contents forward, so the stage can run without the criteria it is meant to apply.
Regenerating criteria reopens a decision the team already made, and comparing two sets adds work without improving the scores.

Correct. A new conversation starts with nothing from the previous stage, so anything the next step depends on has to be carried across explicitly. Restating the criteria and supplying the partner information makes the scoring reproducible and traceable.
